_what_this_is: The correctness pin for the Triton kernels, and the ONLY part of it that runs
on a machine with no GPU and no Triton installed. These kernels are
bit-identical to stepping.py because their expression grouping survives
Triton's MLIR pipeline -- which is held EMPIRICALLY by the byte gate, not by
construction. A Triton version bump is therefore a correctness event, and
this file is what makes it impossible for one to become routine by omission.
kernel_source_sha256 is the sha256 of the SHIPPED kernels.py. The test that
compares it to the live file is what makes the kernel uneditable without
invalidating this record -- and the record cannot be re-cut without re-running
the gate whose verdict it carries. That coupling is the whole mechanism.
The pyproject extra `fdtd-gpu-triton` pins triton>=3.1,<3.2 as a RANGE. The
solver is not the correctness pin: it only stops a wildly wrong version
installing silently far away from anyone who would notice. This file is the
pin that bites.
_why_the_host_is_hashed_too: The kernel is not the whole of what the gate certifies. launch.py chooses the
Yee sub-lattice, binds the coefficient pointers, and decides the SIGMA_IS_VOLUME
constexpr -- each of them a silent wrong answer if it changes. coverage.py
decides whether the kernel runs at all.

_what_this_is: THE DRIVER SEAM, wired 2026-08-14. Before this round nothing dispatched:
fastpath.plan_fast_path returned None on every branch and driver.active_step_path
read 'array' on every run. It now returns a FastPathPlan the driver consults at
seven call sites, and this entry records the SHAPE of that seam -- which slots it
can run, what it refuses, and what the wiring hashes to.
IT IS NOT A CERTIFICATION. No gate in this file was run through these consults;
every one installed its plans by monkeypatching driver module globals from a
probe. That is why dispatch_by_default is FALSE and why an opt-in environment
variable is the only way to reach a kernel. The driver-route gate named in
what_would_certify_this is what turns this record into evidence, and flipping
the default is a one-line change gated on it.
The two digests are the WELD: they are the bytes of the wiring this shape
describes, so the seam cannot drift without invalidating this entry -- the same
discipline host_sha256 applies to the kernel package.

the GPU host, one pinned RTX A6000. Real mp.Simulation objects lifted through
from_meep.lift_simulation, stepped by FdtdDriver.run through the seven
consults, compared against the same builder's driver pinned with

spectrum, at every rung of a x4 checkpoint ladder, not only at the end.
IT DID NOT CERTIFY THE SHIPPED CONFIGURATION. It found a defect the
per-kernel gates could not see, because every one of them installs a
subnormal policy on both executors before it compiles anything and a user's
run installs none. See executor_policy_split below: that is the headline,
and dispatch_by_default stays False because of it.
Results live under parity/meep_gpu/results/ and .gitignore excludes that
tree, so the numbers are transcribed here and the directory named in

executor_policy_split.finding: AS SHIPPED, DISPATCH IS NOT BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE ARRAY PATH. A plain lift_simulation + TRIDENT_FDTD_TRITON=1 run installs NO subnormal policy: CuPy compiles its array kernels with its own -ftz=true (flush) and Triton compiles with no ftz attribute (IEEE keep). The two executors then disagree on exactly one value class, and an FDTD amplifies one such disagreement.
executor_policy_split.flush_is_not_an_option_in_process: install_subnormal_policy('flush') RAISES SubnormalPolicyUnattainable on this host: CuPy 13.5.1's CUB reduction accelerators are fixed at import and keep subnormals, so flush needs CUPY_ACCELERATORS='' set before CuPy is imported. Measured this round.
executor_policy_split.forensics: at the first divergent rung every differing element sits at or beside the subnormal range: largest differing magnitudes 1.9e-30 (pml_2d), 3.7e-35 (pml_3d), 1.9e-27 (dispersive_2d), against a smallest normal float32 of 1.18e-38 and fields of order 1. The first differing element is repeatedly -0.0 against 0.0, which is the signed-zero signature of an underflow one executor flushed and the other kept.
executor_policy_split.measured_keep: with install_subnormal_policy('keep') driving host, CuPy and Triton, ALL EIGHT dispatching cases are byte-identical in the complete final state and in every flux spectrum, at every rung of the ladder -- up to 4,202,496 uint32 words on pml_3d -- while the launch counters prove the kernels ran
executor_policy_split.measured_ship: 6 of the 7 dispatching cases diverge; first divergence at 16 steps (pml_3d) and 64 steps (the rest), inside the 8-64-step window the families are certified over. cylindrical is the only dispatching case that holds for its whole run.
executor_policy_split.this_is_not_the_subnormal_question_that_: The settled question was whether the families certified under 'keep' are covered when the SHIPPED default resolves to flush -- answered yes, transitively, by the conformance gate. This is a different fact: under the shipped default no policy is installed AT ALL, so the two executors do not share one, and 'both flush identically' was never true of a real run.
executor_policy_split.why_no_gate_saw_it: every per-kernel and composition gate calls install_ftz_strip() (or installs the policy through the env seam) BEFORE any compile, so both executors are driven to one policy for the whole gate. That is correct for certifying arithmetic and it is exactly the condition a user's run does not satisfy. The claim the gates support is 'the kernel computes the same bits UNDER A UNIFORM POLICY', and nothing had connected that to 'a user gets the same answer'.

MEASURED: one record licensed arm=FMA_V1 basis='measured' with zero refusals under keep, flush and match_meep alike. DROPPED rather than refusing the whole plan: a None probe makes the complex predicates refuse by name, which is the array path for the complex arms and no change at all for a run with no complex storage.
refuses.mirror_fold: A FOLD REFUSES THE WHOLE PLAN, read from the grid (Grid.is_mirrored / has_symmetry) and not from which arms the composer selected. refuses.uncertified_device: A READABLE compute capability outside validated_compute_capabilities refuses the whole plan by name. Same argument as the Triton version rung on the other half of the codegen input: Triton emits PTX for an architecture, so an arch no gate ran on invalidates the bit-identity claims wholesale. An UNREADABLE device is recorded as unknown and NOT refused -- refusing on a fact that was not read would be asserting it.

MEASURED on the GPU host with the FPU flushing: np.float32(1e-45) is 0x00000000 (the float64->float32 conversion is an SSE result and is flushed); a subnormal built by BIT PATTERN survives in memory as 0x00004000 but compares equal to zero and float() of it is 0.0 (DAZ zeroes it on read); and over the gate's own discriminating operand class -- 24 (a,b,c) rows spanning 0x00000001, 0x00004000, 0x00080000 and 1.0 against 0.25/-0.5/1.0 and +-0.0 -- the exact-fma oracle and the two-rounding product agree on 24/24 rows, where under keep those rows DO separate the FMA_V1 and NAIVE arms. CORRECTION 2026-08-15: this sentence used to say they were the ONLY rows that separate the arms under keep, and that is measurably false -- it was a statement about the rows the gate happened to carry, not about the arithmetic. All-NORMAL operands whose PRODUCT underflows separate them too, under both policies: zr = 0x00800000 (min normal) times c = 0xb3000000 (-2^-25) with z_im = -1.0 gives NAIVE re = 0x00000000 against FMA_V1 re = 0x80000000, because the single-rounded fma keeps the exact underflowing product's sign while the two-rounding form loses it to the -0.0 cross term (24 of 288 words over a 144-row all-normal set under keep, 36 under flush; reproduced in hardware float32 plus exact float64, no emulation). The false premise mattered: it is what made 'flush destroys the discriminators, therefore the arms coincide' look like it followed. It does not, and the probe now carries the all-normal underflowing class (gate_triton_complex._NORMAL_UNDERFLOWING_ZR) so every pattern discriminates under flush as well as keep. Nothing about the eight families' flush verdict changes -- their subnormal LEGS still have no operands on a flushing host, which is the actual reason stated at the head of this entry. Its flip is licensed by the POINT repair alone - correct, because there are no images. The gate's 'unfolded_product' structural leg asks that predicate rather than reading its comment, and meep_gpu/test_folded_deposit_closure.py pins the limit so it is a fact in the suite, not a sentence here.
triton_folded_deposit_closure_device_gat._the_armed_control: on_plane_Ez_row1_CONTROL reproduces the 2026-08-30 placement (source at centre) and is EXPECTED to be vacuous for the closure: leg B does not diverge, it is not counted, and the gate REFUSES to release if it ever stops behaving that way. A protocol that cannot see a vacuous case is not a protocol. It still needs the POINT repair - its leg C diverges - which is exactly why a run that only asked 'does it match the array path?' passed and licensed nothing about the closure.
triton_folded_deposit_closure_device_gat._why_the_digests_start_unbound: This entry was authored with every digest set to 64 zeroes, which no file can hash to. rebind_triton_welds.py fills them FROM THE ARTIFACT's own imported_source_sha256 and only when that artifact says released; if it does not bind, the zeroes stand and test_triton_weld_contract.py's strict byte comparison goes RED. The entry therefore cannot enter the record asserting a device result nobody measured - it fails closed rather than open.
triton_folded_deposit_closure_device_gat._why_this_weld_exists: The 2026-08-30 round flipped CARRIES_DEPOSIT_REPAIR False->True on three Triton products and offered probe_triton_symmetry_composition as the device evidence. That evidence is VACUOUS for this mechanism and the gate MEASURES it rather than asserting it (structural leg 'prior_evidence'): that probe plans with fuse=False, so the flag was inert in it; only 2 of its 6 cases declare a source at all; and its source sits at the grid centre, which on a mirrored axis IS the mirror plane, so the deposit is its own image and a point repair is exact there BY CONSTRUCTION. This weld is the evidence that flip was missing.
triton_folded_deposit_closure_device_gat.purpose: Device byte gate for the FOLDED DEPOSIT IMAGE CLOSURE. On a folded grid the deposit point and its mirror images are different cells and the post-injection fills write images of the deposit, so a POINT-ONLY repair leaves those images carrying the uninjected value. This gate runs three legs per case against the CuPy array path - A: the shipped closure (must be bit-identical), B: a point-only repair (MUST diverge or the case is vacuous), C: no repair at all (must diverge) - and counts only the cases whose leg B actually diverged.
